explanation_en: Derived from military terminology (to storm a fortress), this idiom is used figuratively to describe a place, service, or product that is suddenly overwhelmed by a massive influx of eager customers or visitors. It is commonly used with the verb 'être' ('être pris d'assaut').

examples.en_text: As soon as the sales opened, the department stores were taken by storm by customers.
examples.target_text: Dès l'ouverture des soldes, les grands magasins ont été pris d'assaut par les clients.

examples.en_text: In summer, the beaches in the south of France are rushed by tourists.
examples.target_text: En été, les plages du sud de la France sont prises d'assaut par les touristes.

examples.en_text: The website was stormed as soon as the tickets for the concert went on sale.
examples.target_text: Le site internet a été pris d'assaut dès la mise en vente des billets pour le concert.

examples.en_text: Because of the train strike, the buses were rushed this morning.
examples.target_text: À cause de la grève des trains, les bus ont été pris d'assaut ce matin.

examples.en_text: This bakery is taken by storm every Sunday morning for its excellent croissants.
examples.target_text: Cette boulangerie est prise d'assaut chaque dimanche matin pour ses excellents croissants.

examples.en_text: With the arrival of snow, the ski resorts were rushed this weekend.
examples.target_text: Avec l'arrivée de la neige, les stations de ski ont été prises d'assaut ce week-end.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to take on scale,' this expression is widely used to describe a phenomenon, trend, or movement that is growing in size, influence, or importance. It is an elegant alternative to 'grandir' or 'se développer' and is common in news and formal discussions.

examples.en_text: The protest against the new law is gaining momentum across the country.
examples.target_text: La manifestation contre la nouvelle loi prend de l'ampleur dans tout le pays.

examples.en_text: Our recycling project is gaining momentum and attracting new partners.
examples.target_text: Notre projet de recyclage prend de l'ampleur et attire de nouveaux partenaires.

examples.en_text: The rumor about his resignation gained momentum on social media this morning.
examples.target_text: La rumeur sur sa démission a pris de l'ampleur sur les réseaux sociaux ce matin.

examples.en_text: Teleworking has been gaining momentum for a few years.
examples.target_text: Le télétravail prend de l'ampleur depuis quelques années.

examples.en_text: If this dispute gains momentum, it will be difficult to reach an agreement.
examples.target_text: Si cette dispute prend de l'ampleur, il sera difficile de trouver un accord.

examples.en_text: This music festival is gaining momentum every year and attracting more and more people.
examples.target_text: Ce festival de musique prend de l'ampleur chaque année et attire de plus en plus de monde.

explanation_en: This verb means to re-establish a connection, relationship, or tie with someone, a place, or a tradition after a period of separation. It is frequently used with abstract nouns like 'la tradition', 'le succès', or 'ses racines' (roots). It is a key B2/C1 vocabulary item for discussing cultural or personal reconnections.

examples.en_text: After years of silence, I finally decided to reconnect with my childhood friend.
examples.target_text: Après des années de silence, j'ai enfin décidé de renouer avec mon ami d'enfance.

examples.en_text: During the holidays, she wants to reconnect with nature and go on long hikes.
examples.target_text: Pendant les vacances, elle veut renouer avec la nature et faire de longues randonnées.

examples.en_text: The company hopes to return to success after a difficult year.
examples.target_text: L'entreprise espère renouer avec le succès après une année difficile.

examples.en_text: He took advantage of the end-of-year holidays to reconnect with his family.
examples.target_text: Il a profité des fêtes de fin d'année pour renouer avec sa famille.

examples.en_text: I would really like to get back into playing the piano, but I lack the time.
examples.target_text: J'aimerais beaucoup renouer avec la pratique du piano, mais je manque de temps.

examples.en_text: Did you manage to reconnect with your former co-workers?
examples.target_text: Est-ce que tu as réussi à renouer avec tes anciens collègues de travail ?

explanation_en: This transitional phrase is used to shift the topic of conversation or a news broadcast to a new subject. It implies moving logically from one point to the next. It should not be confused with 'en venir aux mains' (to come to blows).

examples.en_text: After analyzing the results, we move on to the question of the budget for next year.
examples.target_text: Après avoir analysé les résultats, on en vient à la question du budget pour l'année prochaine.

examples.en_text: Now that this point is clear, we move on to the main topic of our meeting.
examples.target_text: Maintenant que ce point est clair, on en vient au sujet principal de notre réunion.

examples.en_text: After long negotiations, we finally come to the signing of the contract.
examples.target_text: Après de longues négociations, on en vient enfin à la signature du contrat.

examples.en_text: With all these delays, we come to wonder if the project will be finished on time.
examples.target_text: Avec tous ces retards, on en vient à se demander si le projet sera terminé à temps.

examples.en_text: After introducing the characters, we move on to the heart of the story.
examples.target_text: Après avoir présenté les personnages, on en vient au cœur de l'histoire.

examples.en_text: After this historical introduction, we move on to recent events.
examples.target_text: Après cette introduction historique, on en vient aux faits récents.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression is commonly used in news reports to describe where a moving vehicle finally stopped, especially after an accident, crash, or loss of control. It adds a dramatic, narrative touch to the description of a trajectory. It is highly specific to transport and accident reporting.

examples.en_text: After sliding on the black ice, the car came to a halt in a ditch.
examples.target_text: Après avoir glissé sur le verglas, la voiture a terminé sa course dans un fossé.

examples.en_text: The ball crossed the entire field before ending up in the back of the net.
examples.target_text: Le ballon a traversé tout le terrain avant de terminer sa course au fond du filet.

examples.en_text: The old space station ended its run in the Pacific Ocean.
examples.target_text: La vieille station spatiale a terminé sa course dans l'océan Pacifique.

examples.en_text: The marble rolled under the sofa and came to a halt against the wall.
examples.target_text: La bille a roulé sous le canapé et a terminé sa course contre le mur.

examples.en_text: The broken-down train gently came to a halt just before the station.
examples.target_text: Le train en panne a doucement terminé sa course juste avant la gare.

examples.en_text: The wheel came off the bike and came to a halt in the middle of the road.
examples.target_text: La roue s'est détachée du vélo et a terminé sa course au milieu de la route.

explanation_en: This is a formal collocation meaning to help or rescue someone in danger or distress. It is often used in legal, medical, or emergency contexts (e.g., 'non-assistance à personne en danger'). It is more formal and precise than simply saying 'aider'.

examples.en_text: The witnesses of the accident immediately ran to provide assistance to the injured.
examples.target_text: Les témoins de l'accident ont immédiatement couru pour porter secours aux blessés.

examples.en_text: Sea rescuers are trained to provide assistance in difficult conditions.
examples.target_text: Les sauveteurs en mer sont formés pour porter secours dans des conditions difficiles.

examples.en_text: If you see someone in danger in the street, you must provide them with assistance.
examples.target_text: Si tu vois quelqu'un en danger dans la rue, tu dois lui porter secours.

examples.en_text: The helicopter took off quickly to provide assistance to the lost hikers.
examples.target_text: L'hélicoptère a décollé rapidement pour porter secours aux randonneurs égarés.

examples.en_text: During the flood, all the neighbors mobilized to provide us with assistance.
examples.target_text: Pendant l'inondation, tous les voisins se sont mobilisés pour nous porter secours.

examples.en_text: The doctor immediately understood that it was necessary to provide assistance to this patient.
examples.target_text: Le médecin a tout de suite compris qu'il fallait porter secours à cette patiente.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase is a more elegant, journalistic synonym for 'pour le moment' or 'actuellement'. It is used to describe a temporary state of affairs that might change in the future. It is highly common in news reporting and formal writing.

examples.en_text: For the time being, flights are still scheduled, but the weather could change quickly.
examples.target_text: Pour l'heure, les vols sont maintenus, mais la météo pourrait changer rapidement.

examples.en_text: We haven't received the results yet, so, for the time being, we have to wait.
examples.target_text: Nous n'avons pas encore reçu les résultats, donc, pour l'heure, nous devons attendre.

examples.en_text: For the time being, I am living with my parents while waiting to find an apartment.
examples.target_text: Pour l'heure, j'habite chez mes parents en attendant de trouver un appartement.

examples.en_text: The project is on hold for the time being because we are short on budget.
examples.target_text: Le projet est en pause pour l'heure, car nous manquons de budget.

examples.en_text: For the time being, the doctor has advised me not to do any sports.
examples.target_text: Pour l'heure, le médecin m'a conseillé de ne pas faire de sport.

examples.en_text: I don't want to make any important decisions for the time being.
examples.target_text: Je ne veux pas prendre de décision importante pour l'heure.

explanation_en: This expression means to re-establish the truth or correct a narrative by presenting the actual facts. It is often used when there is conflicting information or propaganda, and one party wants to clarify what actually happened. It is a sophisticated alternative to 'dire la vérité'.

examples.en_text: After all these false rumors in the newspapers, are they setting the record straight in their latest article?
examples.target_text: Après toutes ces fausses rumeurs dans les journaux, rétablissent-ils les faits dans leur dernier article ?

examples.en_text: The directors were accused of lying; are they setting the record straight during this press conference?
examples.target_text: Les directeurs ont été accusés de mensonge ; rétablissent-ils les faits lors de cette conférence de presse ?

examples.en_text: This documentary is highly anticipated: are the historians finally setting the record straight about this event?
examples.target_text: Ce documentaire est très attendu : les historiens rétablissent-ils enfin les faits sur cet événement ?

examples.en_text: Facing the opposition's accusations, are the ministers setting the record straight with these new figures?
examples.target_text: Face aux accusations de l'opposition, les ministres rétablissent-ils les faits avec ces nouveaux chiffres ?

examples.en_text: Now that the truth is known, are they setting the record straight with their colleagues?
examples.target_text: Maintenant que la vérité est connue, rétablissent-ils les faits auprès de leurs collègues ?

examples.en_text: In their official report, are the investigators setting the record straight concerning the accident?
examples.target_text: Dans leur rapport officiel, les enquêteurs rétablissent-ils les faits concernant l'accident ?

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to favor, highlight, or give a prominent position to something or someone. It is widely used in cultural, artistic, and culinary contexts to describe what is being showcased or emphasized.

examples.en_text: This film festival gives pride of place to young directors.
examples.target_text: Ce festival de cinéma fait la part belle aux jeunes réalisateurs.

examples.en_text: The restaurant's new menu gives pride of place to local products.
examples.target_text: Le nouveau menu du restaurant fait la part belle aux produits locaux.

examples.en_text: This travel magazine gives pride of place to nature photos.
examples.target_text: Ce magazine de voyage fait la part belle aux photos de nature.

examples.en_text: The art exhibition gave pride of place to contemporary artists.
examples.target_text: L'exposition d'art faisait la part belle aux artistes contemporains.

examples.en_text: Our next project will give pride of place to teamwork.
examples.target_text: Notre prochain projet fera la part belle au travail d'équipe.

examples.en_text: The renovation of the house gives pride of place to natural light.
examples.target_text: La rénovation de la maison fait la part belle à la lumière naturelle.

explanation_en: This expression is used when an activity, situation, or feeling resumes with greater force or intensity than before. It is very common in both spoken and written French, often used for weather, arguments, illnesses, or trends. A common pitfall is misspelling 'belle' or trying to masculinize it as 'beau'.

examples.en_text: After a short lull, the rain is starting up again with even more intensity.
examples.target_text: Après une courte accalmie, la pluie repart de plus belle.

examples.en_text: After two days of rest, the project is starting up again with renewed energy.
examples.target_text: Après deux jours de repos, le projet repart de plus belle.

examples.en_text: They had calmed down, but the argument is starting up again even worse than before.
examples.target_text: Ils s'étaient calmés, mais la dispute repart de plus belle.

examples.en_text: As soon as the crisis is over, the economy will bounce back stronger than ever.
examples.target_text: Dès que la crise sera passée, l'économie repartira de plus belle.

examples.en_text: The music stopped for a moment, then it started up again even louder.
examples.target_text: La musique s'est arrêtée un instant, puis elle est repartie de plus belle.

examples.en_text: Since this morning, the rumors about his departure are starting up again with a vengeance.
examples.target_text: Depuis ce matin, les rumeurs sur son départ repartent de plus belle.

explanation_en: Literally used for things destroyed by fire, this expression is also widely used figuratively to describe hopes, money, plans, or efforts that vanish completely without result. It is a common idiom across all registers, from news reports to daily conversations.

examples.en_text: All of his future plans went up in smoke after the company's bankruptcy.
examples.target_text: Tous ses projets d'avenir sont partis en fumée après la faillite de l'entreprise.

examples.en_text: Unfortunately, the old barn behind the house went up in smoke during the storm.
examples.target_text: Malheureusement, la vieille grange derrière la maison est partie en fumée pendant l'orage.

examples.en_text: All our illusions went up in smoke when we saw the exam results.
examples.target_text: Toutes nos illusions sont parties en fumée quand nous avons vu les résultats de l'examen.

examples.en_text: All his research work went up in smoke because of a computer bug.
examples.target_text: Tout son travail de recherche est parti en fumée à cause d'un bug informatique.

examples.en_text: The millions of euros invested in this project went up in smoke in a few months.
examples.target_text: Les millions d'euros investis dans ce projet sont partis en fumée en quelques mois.

examples.en_text: Her chance of getting the promotion went up in smoke after this serious mistake.
examples.target_text: Sa chance d'obtenir la promotion est partie en fumée après cette grave erreur.

explanation_en: Originating from driving (where 'point mort' means neutral gear), this idiom describes a situation, project, or negotiation that is completely stalled and making no progress. It is highly common in business, politics, and everyday life.

examples.en_text: The town hall renovation project is at a standstill due to a lack of budget.
examples.target_text: Le projet de rénovation de la mairie est au point mort à cause du manque de budget.

examples.en_text: Since he refused that promotion, his career has been at a standstill.
examples.target_text: Depuis qu'il a refusé cette promotion, sa carrière est au point mort.

examples.en_text: Negotiations between the union and management have been at a standstill since last night.
examples.target_text: Les négociations entre le syndicat et la direction sont au point mort depuis hier soir.

examples.en_text: The police investigation is at a standstill because there are no new witnesses.
examples.target_text: L'enquête de police est au point mort car il n'y a aucun nouveau témoin.

examples.en_text: I'm trying to write my first novel, but for now, my writing is at a standstill.
examples.target_text: J'essaie d'écrire mon premier roman, mais pour l'instant, mon écriture est au point mort.

examples.en_text: Our discussion about the holidays is at a standstill; we can't seem to agree.
examples.target_text: Notre discussion sur les vacances est au point mort, nous n'arrivons pas à nous mettre d'accord.
